title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 26, 2026
headline: Jalen Brooks is out for the year; Jeremiyah Love and Max Melton are expected at Wednesday's practice, and Jacoby Brissett remains the starter despite red-zone struggles.
summary: LaFleur said Jalen Brooks will have surgery and is out for the season after playing through an injury that surfaced in the first quarter. The replacement plan is by committee, with Reggie Virgil getting reps, Kendrick Bourne able to play some Max, and Simi Fehoko handling multiple roles. He expects Jeremiyah Love and Max Melton back at practice Wednesday, while Walter Nolen is probably not ready for Wednesday. Defensively, he attributed the three big plays (a 62-yard scramble, a screen, and an over-aggressive cloud-technique run) to correctable details rather than scheme. On offense, he said Jacoby Brissett is still the starter and that finishing drives in the red zone, which has fallen to last in the league, is on the coaching staff. He was positive on Bam Knight, who keeps a role even if Love returns, and he said Brissett has no injury concerns this week. He would not discuss a role change for a player with a back spasm, saying more would be known after a Tuesday workout. He also declined to speculate on James Conner's status beyond saying Conner knows his body.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Monday, October 26th | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski says Zachariah Branch's role will keep growing after a strong Week 7 win; Mike Penix Jr. praised for learning and ball security, with no injury news given.
summary: Stefanski opened by praising the physicality of the Week 7 win over San Francisco, citing a +4 turnover margin and the team's play on both sides of the ball, then turned the page to a division opponent. On Mike Penix Jr., he said quarterbacks improve with more starts and varied looks, and that Penix is gathering experience against different coverages, pressures and red-zone philosophies. He described Penix's shift to under-center and pistol looks as an evolution of things he has run before, and credited the offensive line for keeping him clean with zero sacks. Asked about the team's identity, he said it is about being physical, citing receivers cracking safeties and linemen moving defenders. He praised safety Jessie Bates III as a ball-aware veteran who leads by example. Stefanski said he doesn't get caught up in statistics, though he is aware of the turnover margin, which is minus three after seven weeks and improving. He said starting fast comes from clear plans and tools like a competitive period at the start of practice. Finally, he said Zachariah Branch played very well, delivering a big kickoff return, reverse plays and pass-game production, and that his role will continue to grow. No injury updates were given.

signals.note: Coach praised his big return, reverse, and pass-game plays and said his role will expand, which could mean more touches and snaps.

signals.claim: Penix is getting better with each start and gaining experience against varied defenses
signals.note: Coach framed Penix's development and ball security positively, supporting his reliability as a streaming option, though no specific usage change was stated.
signals.quote: I think that's what I see from Mike is stacking these games

signals.note: Praised as a ball-hawking veteran leader, which supports his usual role but offers no specific fantasy change.
signals.quote: Guys trust him. His teammates trust him.

The team plans to address slow starts with a competitive period at the start of practice, game-day or weekly messaging, and clear early-game plans.

title: Jesse Minter Reflects on Week 7 Loss, Areas for Improvement
headline: Lamar Jackson's status for the Buffalo game stays unresolved until Wednesday, while Minter focuses on the Ravens' second-half collapses.
summary: Minter said he was disappointed in how the Ravens played in the second half of the loss and framed the next ten games as a chance to decide what kind of team they will be. He called Lamar Jackson's return a work in progress: Jackson is working hard, got some work in late last week, and should be in a decent spot, but the team will know much more Wednesday. He declined to discuss the details of Jackson's ankle, and said that once he is healthy enough to play, he will play. Minter said the team has been inconsistent in the second half, admitted the numbers show they have not made the right adjustments, and pointed to all three phases and halftime preparation as areas to fix. On the run game, he said there is no single common denominator; the issues come from what the team asks its younger linemen and tight ends to do, and the offensive line has been in flux. He praised offensive coordinator Declan for managing 16 or 17 offensive line combinations, the missing starting quarterback, and Zay Flowers missing a game, and said Declan has strong opening scripts but must improve consistency and adjustments. Minter also said he won't use Jackson's absence as an excuse for offensive struggles, and that the short week before a road game in Buffalo is a factor in how they bring him back.

injuries.detail: Still working toward a return from an ankle injury; coach said the team will know more Wednesday. He got some work in late last week and was expected to be in a decent spot. Minter declined to discuss details.

signals.claim: Availability for the Buffalo game is undetermined and will be clarified Wednesday; he will play when healthy enough.
signals.note: His status is the biggest swing factor for the offense, and the Wednesday update will set expectations for the short-week game.
signals.quote: we'll know a lot more on Wednesday

topics.detail: Minter acknowledged the team has been outscored badly after halftime and said adjustments, halftime preparation, and third-quarter execution need work. He framed the issue as an all-phase problem.

Minter said there is no single common denominator for the recent run-game struggles. He pointed to the schemes, the asks of younger linemen and tight ends, and offensive line turnover, while saying the line's changes are not an excuse.
Minter said defending top receivers varies play to play, with differences in coverage and alignment. He said the problem starts with coaching and putting players in better positions.
Minter praised Declan for managing many injuries and offensive line combinations in his first season as play caller. He said Declan still needs to improve consistency and in-game adjustments.

Minter said the team needs someone to rally players on the sideline and that some leaders are struggling with their own play. He said the team tries to hold players accountable while avoiding public finger-pointing.

title: Dave Canales reflects on Panthers' run defense
headline: Canales says the run defense is being reworked and calls more Lathan Ransom playing time a possibility.
summary: Canales said the Panthers are working on run defense problems but declined to detail the specific adjustments. He said the coaching staff needs to execute better as a group, coach it more collectively, and build a plan so players feel prepared and ready to attack the concepts they will see. He also said the team needs to take away the run game so opponents have to go to other options. When asked about Lathan Ransom, who saw limited snaps until the Bucs game was out of hand, Canales said more playing time is a possibility. He praised Ransom's physicality and said he has been showing up for the team, while noting that Ransom missed a couple of tackles and that the staff has personnel and scheme options to weigh. Canales also said the Bucs had a plan and did not simply hand the ball to Baker Mayfield, who played well and was scrappy. The transcript is partial and ends mid-thought, so the coach's full comments are not captured.

signals.claim: Could see a bigger role on the back end of the defense, which the coach called a possibility.
signals.note: A larger role on defense would add snaps and potential tackle opportunities, but the coach hedged and no change is confirmed.
signals.quote: that's a possibility

topics.detail: Canales said the team is working through run defense problems and making adjustments in coaching and execution, without revealing specifics. The Bucs' run game was the main concern in the last game.

He also gave a garbled update on a player named 'Doug' (likely a different player) who he said will definitely miss this week. He praised the defense's red zone play, crediting confidence, film review, and stopping both runs and passes, and said he expects that to carry forward. He said the offensive line played well and that Amarius Mims is the best tackle he has seen this year. On Joe Burrow, he described the quarterback's preparation and accuracy in detail, and said the go-ball to Ja'Marr Chase matched a practice rep. Taylor credited Chase with setting the tone at halftime, and said Tee Higgins's second-half catch set up a scoring drive. He called Jack Endries ready for a bigger role due to injuries at tight end, and said Endries will get starting-group reps with Burrow. He said Cam Grandy is returning to the roster, which will require a corresponding move, and he declined to elaborate on the penalty situation. On Shemar Stewart, he said the defensive lineman was inactive this week but is improving and doing everything right.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: October 26th, 2026
headline: Quinshon Judkins is trending up with a better run-game setup and Mason Graham is still working back from a hard-fought return, while Jared Verse's offsides exit was partly rotation and partly accountability.
summary: Monken downplayed the narrative around Deshaun Watson's fourth-quarter game-winning drives, stressing that the team must start faster and that the focus is on the Pittsburgh week. He credited the run game's improvement to more consistent game plans, players who are more familiar with the scheme, and more auxiliary runs and skill-player touches, with Watson part of that. On Quinshon Judkins, Monken said the team finally gave him room to run, and he praised his power and his downhill running. He said Jared Verse's offside penalty and sideline exit was a mix of rotation and accountability, tied to teams using a double cadence. On Watson's interception, Monken said Denzel Boston's coverage was a man-coverage look where the inside receiver was shut off and there was no other throwing window, and he blamed the team for not getting to the spot first. Monken said the 12-men penalty on a punt was a failure by the player on the field, the coaching staff, and the special teams unit. Mason Graham is sore after returning from an injury and should keep improving over the coming weeks. The coach said no decision had been made on the quarterbacks coming up, which depends on health and roster management. Monken also said the team is working on its slow starts, especially on defense, and he discussed the physical culture the team needs against Pittsburgh.

injuries.detail: Returned to the game after leaving, is sore, and is expected to take a few weeks to get back to full strength.

signals.claim: The run game is getting him better looks with more room to run, and he is more explosive than before.
signals.note: Better blocking and more downhill space support more efficient rushing and more trust in his workload.

signals.claim: His early exit after the offside penalty was partly a rotation decision and partly accountability, so the coach may not overreact to it.
signals.note: A rotation-based sideline exit could cost him some snaps, but the coach downplayed it as a long-term concern.
signals.quote: A little both.

signals.claim: The team has to improve as a whole, including his play, and the start-of-game struggles must be fixed.
signals.note: Consistency and early-game efficiency still matter for his weekly floor, despite his late-game success.
signals.quote: He can certainly play better.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s special teams unit: ‘[The] group has done a real good job’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims Jr. needs more offensive touches despite his kick return role, and Jonah Coleman is earning more work after explosive Week 7 touches.
summary: Payton said Jonah Coleman played well in his third NFL game and that his touches were explosive. He framed more touches as something Coleman has to earn, and said Coleman has done a good job of that. On Marvin Mims Jr., Payton said the team moved him back to kick returns partly because of how the opponent was kicking off, which led Denver to use a single returner. Payton said Mims is one of the team's explosive playmakers and that the team needs to get him more touches on offense. He also credited the special teams group, which he called the quickest way to improve a team, and said the unit has done a real good job. On the Chiefs rivalry, Payton said he doesn't see rivalry weeks in the NFL, only important divisional games. He declined to get into the reverse play from last night beyond saying he had been taking too many unimportant questions. A question about a player's pressure rate got a garbled player name, and Payton's praise for that player's rising play and snap counts could not be tied to a roster player with confidence.

signals.claim: Coleman is earning more touches at running back after explosive usage in Week 7
signals.note: Payton's praise of his explosive touches and the idea that more work is earned points to a growing role behind the RB rotation.
signals.quote: the touches he had were explosive

signals.claim: Mims will get more touches on offense, not just on kick returns
signals.note: Payton said the team plans to get Mims more offensive touches, which could add receiving or rushing volume beyond his return duties.
signals.quote: we need to get him more touches on offense and we'll do that

Denver went to a single kick returner after the opponent's kickoff approach changed, and the early return to midfield gave the team a boost to start the game.
Payton said he doesn't see rivalry weeks in the NFL and treats divisional games as important, but not as special rivalry games.

title: Campbell on Branch & Reed
headline: Ennis Rakestraw (ankle) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) are both expected back at Thursday's practice after likely sitting Wednesday; the run game remains the main concern.
summary: Campbell praised the defense for a second straight strong outing, citing better coverage, pressure up front, a sack of Hutchinson early, and a run defense that held up while limiting the pass game. He singled out Khalil Dorsey, D.J. Reed, Chuck Clark, Tyleik Williams, Rock Ya-Sin, Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, and said the red-zone work and the goal-line stop after a turnover were strong. On offense he said the Lions ran the ball and got yards but need more efficiency and explosive runs, and that the first and last drives were their best. Penei Sewell was called outstanding, and Campbell said the Lions need to find more ways to get him the ball. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Isaac TeSlaa, Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright were all praised for their blocking and tight-end play. On the run game, Campbell attributed the backfield penetration and negative plays to a mix of technique, missed assignments and youth or rust, and said Cade Mays needs reps after a near-full game return. Ennis Rakestraw has a minor ankle issue and is expected at Thursday's practice, and St. Brown also had an ankle issue that is expected to be fine. The team now turns to Minnesota, a hot opponent at home.

title: Matt LaFleur after loss to the Lions: 'We gotta learn and move on'
headline: Packers lost 20-17 to Detroit; Josh Jacobs looked good in his debut, but Sean Rhyan and Jacob Monk are unlikely to play this week and the running game and red zone still need work.
summary: LaFleur was disappointed by the 20-17 loss to the Lions. He felt the team competed but failed to cash in on good field position after a defensive stop, and a missed field goal hurt. He said the team must move on quickly ahead of a Thursday night home game against a tough opponent. He would not explain or criticize the officiating, saying he wouldn't comment on the penalties and that calls were tough but must be overcome. He praised Josh Jacobs' debut, citing a spectacular touchdown catch on a choice route and some good runs, but said the team still isn't running the ball consistently enough. The team was down to its third center, and John Williams stepped in at center in a hostile environment and handled it well. LaFleur said he would not expect centers Sean Rhyan or Jacob Monk to play this week and could not say about the long term. On the red zone, he said the team must finish plays, that running the ball efficiently is key, and that he regrets not kicking a field goal on fourth down earlier. He also praised the defense, but cited offsides penalties and drops as ongoing problems.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Accountability & Using the Bye Week to Reset | Full Q&A
headline: Ryans owns the tackling, penalty and close-game problems at 2-5; Nico Collins was doubled and Tank Dell gets praise, while David Montgomery's and the other injuries stay unclear entering the bye.
summary: Ryans took ownership of the Texans' fundamentals problems, saying tackling and penalties start with him and that he needs to coach the details better and emphasize them more in practice. He said the team is sitting back instead of wrapping up and playing fast, and that the penalties come from blocking technique and holding. He called the 2-5 start unacceptable, noting five games have been decided in the final possession with only one win, and that the defense has not closed out those games. He said the offense's third-down struggles and the explosive plays allowed are his responsibility to fix, and he pointed to the Giants' physicality as the reason the offensive line and defense lost the line of scrimmage. On Nico Collins, he said the team was doubled because game flow prevented sustained drives, and he expressed confidence in Collins' ability to win contested catches. He gave no update on David Montgomery or the turf toe injury to another player, and said he is taking things one day at a time. He praised C.J. Stroud's season, said Tank Dell has earned his optimism through practice, and said the bye week will be used for evaluation and resetting.

injuries.detail: Ryans said he did not have an update on Montgomery or the other player asked about, who was being evaluated for turf toe.

signals.note: Heavy double coverage limited his targets last game, so his volume depends on whether the offense sustains drives.

signals.note: Ryans gave Stroud high praise and said his play is why the team wins, supporting continued stable QB production.

signals.note: Ryans cited Dell's practice work over the last three weeks rather than a single play, suggesting a continued role in the offense.

Ryans said he expects to keep the current coaching staff and is confident in the offensive and defensive schemes, while acknowledging the need for better execution and adjustments.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 7 recap, Colts at Vikings
headline: Steichen says Daniel Jones remains the starter barring a health issue; Cam Taylor-Britt and Justin Walley were hurt in Week 7, and Micheal Clemons and Alec Pierce are unlikely to start practicing this week.
summary: Steichen opened by saying the team didn't make enough plays to win the Vikings game and that the focus now is Jacksonville, a division road game. He was asked directly whether Daniel Jones is still the starter and said yes, adding that Jones will remain the quarterback unless the coach tells reporters otherwise. He acknowledged Jones needs to play better and that the plan to run the ball had to give way to throwing to score points. Steichen said he has confidence in Jones because of his preparation, leadership, and past success in the system, and that the team has faith in him moving forward. On injuries, he said Justin Walley and Cam Taylor-Britt were hurt in the game and that the team will meet with doctors and update them through the week. Tyler Warren is progressing well but his practice status is still unknown. Steichen said Clemons and Pierce, both on IR, will most likely not begin their practice windows this week. He also said the culture is strong and the locker room is committed to daily improvement. title: Coen on Reset After Bye Week, Correcting Penalties & Creating More Explosives | Press Conference
headline: Brian Thomas Jr. is expected to help in Week 8 after returning to the receiver rotation; Antonio Johnson is TBD and Anton Harrison's season is effectively over, with Walker Little next up on the line.
summary: Coen said every week brings new players stepping up in this receiver group, and he expects Brian Thomas Jr. to help make plays Sunday, adding that the staff will support him and put him in good position. On injuries, he called Antonio Johnson's status TBD and said he couldn't yet say whether Johnson or the other returning player would be available Sunday, though he is excited to see them back on the grass. He called Anton Harrison's situation a bummer, said the team will miss him, and praised Walker Little for stepping up against Houston in both run and pass blocking with a next-man-up mentality. Coen said the staff will evaluate the return of the player coming off IR later this week, and that the offensive line depth remains good. On self-scout, he said offensive penalties in the red zone have been a problem, defenses have allowed too many explosive pass plays, and special teams must improve on punt return and kickoff coverage. On Travis Hunter's offensive snaps, Coen said the staff won't over-rotate him after a good game, and he pointed to the team's wins with Hunter even when his snap count was lower. He said the running game has been efficient but not very explosive, with backs turning blocked-up plays into positives, and the goal is more 15-to-20-yard gains. He said the team is in a reset after the bye, with a division game this week and a stretch of five AFC South games ahead, with full pads coming Wednesday.

He said Fernando Mendoza will play at some point, but not this week, and that there is no timeline. On the quarterback decision, Kubiak said the team's input matters, but the final call is his and will be based on what gives the team the best chance to win. He said the priority is winning the next game while continuing to develop Mendoza. Special teams was described as a bright spot, with Joe DeCamillis praised for his grit and his staff. Kubiak highlighted Dylan Laube's value across special teams and as a third-down back. He also praised Darien Porter's mental toughness and talent as he matures at corner, and said the team is still deciding on a roster move at the end of the week. title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 26 | Press Conference

summary: Hafley described the win over the Jets as an emotional day, pointing to the locker-room reception and his family's presence outside as highlights. He said the team has a young roster with many players who had never won an NFL game, so the win mattered for confidence and belief in the process, though he stressed they must move on quickly. He tied the two aggressive fourth-down decisions and the goal-line stand to the identity he wants: toughness, resiliency and physicality. He credited Willis for quick decisions, ball security, and extending drives, and said Dulcich had a really good game with several tackle-breaking and vertical plays. He also praised the receivers and tight ends for blocking in the run game, and said Hafley's own offensive staff, led by Bobby, is still finding what the offense does well, with a mix of gap, outside zone and varied fullback and tight end alignments. Hafley acknowledged the team let a 21-7 lead slip and called it a learning experience. He wrapped up by saying the focus is on their own development against a strong Patriots team coming in.

He credited Kyler Murray's accuracy and his legs, and said the offense has moved the ball well over the last two games but has not turned that into points. He admitted the coaches share responsibility for the three-and-outs on early runs, and said the offense needs to score more to win at Detroit. On the injury front, Aaron Jones is day-to-day, and several players returning from missed time came back clean. Asked about backfield depth, O'Connell praised DeeJay Dallas for his pass protection and kicking-game work and said Demond Claiborne is developing every week, so he does not see a depth problem for now. He also praised Joe Huber's effort filling in on the interior line, while noting that one-on-one losses there disrupt the pocket. Defensively, he highlighted Levi Drake Rodriguez's instincts and Blake Cashman's growth into the green-dot role. He framed the Lions game as a tough road division test against a high-powered offense.

Glenn defended not calling timeout at the end of the first half, citing the process, the clock, and the possibility of the opponent getting first downs. He said he needs to do better.
Glenn said the carry choice at the one-yard line does not matter as much as scoring there. He said the offense must improve in that situation.

Glenn said the week will center on practice, meetings, and walkthroughs, and the team is tuning out outside noise.

title: WATCH: The MIke McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 8)
headline: McCarthy lifts Spencer Anderson's jumbo-package role, says DeShon Elliott cleared his first game back, and praises Payton Wilson's growth, with Cleveland up Sunday.
summary: McCarthy said the Steelers want their running backs touching the ball and felt good about the distribution in Sunday's 16-10 win over New Orleans in Paris. He credited Spencer Anderson's versatility as a big reason for the jumbo package, saying he wanted to give Anderson a real chance to compete for a job before inserting him at right guard. He called the team's close wins necessary for building confidence and said the road trip went well. On the defense, he said middle linebackers Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen are stepping forward, and Wilson's interception was one of the biggest plays of the game. He said DeShon Elliott got past his first regular-season game in nearly a year, with his snaps managed by a play count. He praised Aaron Rodgers' mental capacity as a key part of his success this year. The coach also said the Browns are already familiar territory after the Week 4 loss, with little change to their depth chart so far, and that the preparation for Cleveland is in its normal Monday phase.

signals.note: The jumbo package with Anderson produced strong run results, so a continued role gives fantasy-relevant run-game lift for the Steelers' backs.

signals.note: A growing role for Wilson in the defense, including splash plays, adds upside for IDP managers.
signals.quote: Payton's plays has been probably one of the biggest plays in the game.

signals.note: McCarthy praised Rodgers' mental capacity as a driver of his success, which supports his QB1 status.

topics.detail: Offensive coordinator Brian Angelico credited the offensive line and backs Jalen Warren and Rico Dowdle for converting short-yardage third downs. He said Anderson's presence gives flexibility alongside Darnell Washington, and that Rico Dowdle looked healthy and fresh.

Special teams coordinator Danny Crossman discussed the end-of-half field goal and kick return struggles. The broadcast noted Caden Wetjen is still developing as a returner. These comments came from Crossman, not McCarthy.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I'm Proud Of Our Style Of Play"
headline: Charles Cross's ankle timetable is unclear, while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet could both return for Monday night.
summary: Macdonald said the team gets an extra prep day, with Wednesday as a recovery-focused day, and explained that he has learned overloading the week can leave players mentally taxed. He credited the offense's turnaround to its style of play, the run game, and third-down execution, while admitting red zone finishing and takeaways still need work. He praised the defense's connected, hard-playing effort and said Nick Emmanwori has handled multiple position-group roles with maturity, though the extra time that requires is significant. On injuries, he said Charles Cross has an ankle injury of unknown length and the team has not discussed IR, while Rashid Shaheed's early returns are positive without a specific timeline. Velus Jones Jr. has a hamstring injury of unknown severity. Macdonald said Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet could both play, or either one could, depending on how their recoveries go.

title: Todd Bowles on Keeping the Same Energy | Press Conference
headline: Bucs leaned on a three-back run game that stayed productive all afternoon, Bucky Irving looks like a workhorse, and Emeka Egbuka is questionable with a concussion and foot injury.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs' plan (control time of possession, run the ball, win turnovers, and make special-teams plays) came together close to how they drew it up. He denied that the team was protecting Baker Mayfield in his first game back; the run game kept working, so they kept running, which limited Mayfield to about 11 passes. He praised Bucky Irving's mental toughness, work ethic, and ability to cut at full speed, saying Irving can carry a starter's load into the fourth quarter. He called Benjamin Chukwuma's first start of the year outstanding and said he has a huge future as a full-time starter. Bowles said the offensive line needs to stay consistent, and that linemen get more motivated when the run game produces. He said the three backs all got downhill and gained yardage. On injuries, Bowles said the group of players tied to the Winfield/Egbuka question is questionable, with a final decision coming Wednesday or Thursday; Egbuka is listed with both a concussion and a foot injury, and Bowles said both contributed about equally to him not playing Sunday. He also said no new injuries came out of the game. Bowles discussed the defense, saying Zyon McCollum's best trait is press coverage and zone vision, and that the defensive line's pressure and coverage on the backside are working together to create sacks and turnovers. He also explained that the team elected to receive after winning the toss because he wanted to establish the run game early and see the offensive line.

Bowles credited the defensive line for generating pressure and sacks, with coverage on the backside helping. Zyon McCollum was praised for press coverage and zone vision, and a blocked extra point returned for two points gave the team momentum.

Bowles said the pregame plan (time of possession, run game, turnovers, special teams) was executed close to the ideal. The team elected to receive after winning the toss to establish the run game early.
Bowles said no new injuries came out of the game and no one was known to be sidelined beyond the questionable players.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/27/26
headline: With Terry McLaurin out, Antonio Williams is the likely beneficiary of more targets, and Trey Amos is back in the secondary.
summary: Quinn opened with injury updates: Trey Amos is returning to practice, Javon Kinlaw is recovering more slowly than hoped from a knee issue, and Marcus Mariota is back at practice. He described the bye as a useful reset, with separate self-scouts for each phase and a collective review, and he wants more consistent fight and intensity for all four quarters. On the staff, Steve Wilks was added to help with defensive game planning early in the week, and Quinn said the timing made sense. He praised Amos's quick return and said the defense doesn't rely on one player to fix the pass defense. On Jayden Daniels, Quinn said that in some games he could be more aggressive into tight windows, but he valued his accuracy and deep-ball placement overall. On the offense, he said the offensive line work during the break centered on strategy, especially run-game finishing and downfield blocking. For the Terry McLaurin absence, Stefon Diggs is healthy and his workload should not change much, but Antonio Williams should see more targets. Quinn also said Jacory Croskey-Merritt is back in the running game alongside another running back, and he gave a groin injury update for a player whose name was unclear in the transcript. Philadelphia is the next opponent, followed by two more conference games, two of them divisional.
